newsitem.title: USA: Whirlpool says long-term strategy sound.
newsitem.headline: Whirlpool says long-term strategy sound.

text.p: Whirlpool Corp, which has been hit by three debt ratings downgrades this month, said Friday its long-term strategy and balance sheet remain strong.
"The downgrades are associated with our lower than expected 1996 performance. We recognize that. We're expecting improvements in our operations in 1997," said company spokesman T.R. Reid.

Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co, which cut ratings on $2.4 billion in debt on Friday, said the downgrade reflects the overall weakening of credit protection measures resulting from persistently weak earnings in key markets combined with heavy investments to establish businesses in new Asian markets.
It follows similar actions by Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service.
Reid said the downgrades do not reflect a lack of confidence in the company's strategy of pushing into new markets, but a desire to see better near-term results as the company executes the strategy.
Reid noted the appliance maker had record operating earnings in its core North America unit in 1996.
